issues.t: Head gasket leaks on the 3.0L
issues.sym: Coolant or oil seeping from the engine, the coolant level dropping, overheating, or white smoke from the exhaust.
issues.why: The B9 Tribeca's 3.0L six develops head gasket leaks at higher mileage. It is the top engine complaint for these years, often around 100,000-140,000 miles, and many owners report it more than once.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test done, and fix leaks before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a crash, the passenger airbag inflator can burst and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: The Tribeca uses a Takata passenger airbag inflator whose propellant breaks down after years of heat and humidity. Subaru recalled 2006-2012 Tribecas in stages.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Subaru dealer or NHTSA right away and get the free inflator replacement.

issues.t: Hood can fly open while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The hood isn't fully latched, pops up, or flies open at speed and blocks your view.
issues.why: Corrosion or hardened grease in the hood latch can stop the secondary catch from engaging. Subaru recalled every Tribeca model year.
issues.next: Make sure the hood is fully closed and check your VIN with a Subaru dealer for the free latch repair.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the timing chain cover and head gaskets
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine, a burning oil smell, or oil coating the front of the engine and the oil cooler area.
issues.why: The 3.6L six can leak oil from the timing chain cover, the oil cooler seal and the head gaskets. Owners report repairs around $1,700-2,500.
issues.next: Have the leak traced before replacing parts, keep the oil topped up, and fix leaks dripping on the exhaust quickly.

issues.t: Overheating that can damage the engine
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant leaks from the radiator, or the engine runs rough or loses power after an overheat.
issues.why: Radiator leaks and failing thermostats lead to overheating. One owner reports an overheat lowered oil pressure enough for the timing chains to skip and damage valves and pistons; others report cracked blocks.
issues.next: Pull over and shut it off if it overheats. Replace a leaking radiator quickly; after a serious overheat, ask for a compression test.

issues.t: Harsh shifting or torque converter failure
issues.sym: Hard shifts between second and third, shuddering, slipping, or warning lights for stability control and cruise along with the check engine light.
issues.why: Owners report transmission software updates for hard shifts, torque converter replacements around 60,000-100,000 miles and some full rebuilds.
issues.next: Ask a Subaru dealer about a transmission software update and change the fluid. If it slips or shudders, get a transmission diagnosis before it gets worse.

issues.t: Transmission may not hold in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The shifter won't come out of Park, or the vehicle rolls while in Park.
issues.why: The parking rod inside the five-speed automatic can come loose on Tribecas built in late June 2013. Subaru replaces the transmission.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and check your VIN with a Subaru dealer.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often
issues.sym: Low beam bulbs (and sometimes brake light bulbs) burn out again and again, or water collects inside the headlight.
issues.why: Frequent low beam bulb failures are among the most reported Tribeca problems. Some owners also find water getting into the headlight housing.
issues.next: Replace bulbs in pairs, handle them without touching the glass, and check the housing for moisture. A leaking housing needs replacing.

issues.t: Front suspension rattle or clunk from sway bar bushings
issues.sym: A rattle or clunk from the front over bumps.
issues.why: Worn front sway bar bushings and links are the most common cause.
issues.next: Have the sway bar bushings and end links checked; it is an inexpensive fix.

issues.t: Worn control arm bushings and struts
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, clunks, a bouncy ride, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: Owners report worn lower control arm bushings and leaking or collapsed struts as these heavy SUVs age.
issues.next: Have the front end inspected, replace worn parts in pairs, and get an alignment.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling
issues.sym: The A/C works on and off, then blows warm.
issues.why: Owners report failed A/C relays, control panels and compressors.
issues.next: Have the relay and controls checked first, since they're much cheaper than a compressor.

issues.t: Water on the passenger floor from a clogged A/C drain
issues.sym: A wet carpet on the front passenger side, often after using the A/C.
issues.why: The A/C drain hose clogs, so condensation backs up into the cabin.
issues.next: Have the drain hose cleared and dry the carpet to prevent mold.

issues.t: Rear differential temperature warning light
issues.sym: The R.DIFF.TEMP light flickers or stays on.
issues.why: Owners report faulty or dirty rear differential temperature sensors causing false warnings.
issues.next: Have the differential oil checked and the sensor and connector cleaned or replaced.

issues.t: Accessory belt tensioner or idler pulley noise
issues.sym: A whine, squeal or chirp from the front of the engine.
issues.why: Belt tensioners and idler pulleys wear out. One owner reports a pulley bolt shearing.
issues.next: Have the tensioner and pulleys checked and replace them with the belt.

issues.t: Misfire from failed ignition coils
issues.sym: Rough running, a flashing check engine light, and a cylinder misfire code.
issues.why: Ignition coils fail on the six-cylinder engines.
issues.next: Have the codes read and replace the failed coil, and plugs if due.

issues.t: Torn CV boots
issues.sym: Grease sprayed inside the wheel, then clicking in turns.
issues.why: The axle boots crack and tear with age.
issues.next: Replace the boot or axle before the joint wears out.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum
issues.sym: A hum or growl that rises with speed.
issues.why: Wheel bearings and hubs wear on this heavy SUV.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked and replace the bad one.

issues.t: Rattling exhaust heat shields
issues.sym: A metallic rattle from under the vehicle or engine bay.
issues.why: Heat shields loosen; Subaru issued a bulletin for one engine bay rattle.
issues.next: Have the shields re-secured.

issues.t: Power window switch or motor failure
issues.sym: A window is slow, stops part way, or won't respond to the switch.
issues.why: Power window switches and motors are common failures.
issues.next: Test the switch first; it is cheaper than a motor.

issues.t: Tailgate struts fail or the tailgate rattles
issues.sym: The tailgate won't stay up or is hard to lift, or it rattles over bumps.
issues.why: The gas support struts lose pressure, and a poorly fitting weatherstrip lets the tailgate rattle.
issues.next: Replace both struts together. Adjust the tailgate stops or seal for a rattle.

issues.t: Front doors won't unlock or open from inside
issues.sym: The front doors don't unlock when shifting to Park, even with the button, or won't open from inside.
issues.why: Owners report failed door lock actuators.
issues.next: Have the door lock actuators checked.

issues.t: Remote start shuts off or works on and off
issues.sym: The factory remote start doesn't start the engine or shuts off after idling.
issues.why: Owners report replacing the remote start control module.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check the remote start module.

issues.t: Power steering leaks or grinding
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips, a groan or grind when turning, or heavier steering.
issues.why: Owners report leaking hoses, steering racks and failing pumps.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and have the leak found.

issues.t: Oil burning on the 3.6L
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, sometimes about a quart every 1,200 miles, and spark plugs come out oily.
issues.why: Owners report some cylinders on the 3.6L burning oil at higher mileage.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and have a compression and leak-down test done.
